goal: Add exclusive per-profile session locking and controlled installed-client smoke coverage.
completed: Added an application-owned exclusive profile-session lease held before materialization through refreshed-credential capture.
Added a mode-0600 runtime lock with no-follow open, owner/permission/type/hardlink checks, immediate contention failure, and release-on-drop.
Added an ignored installed-client smoke test using synthetic credentials and agy --version.
The smoke test passed against installed agy 1.1.2 without authentication or a model request.
Complete local gate passes with 61 automated tests.
nextActions: Review and merge the session-lock pull request, then prepare and execute the controlled two-account validation protocol before enabling any real CLI command.
decisions: Direct refresh-token injection is a viable agy 1.1.2 Linux SSH profile mechanism; the official client continues to own refresh and backend requests.
Real operator-controlled state may be inspected temporarily during authorized research, but independent OAuth enrollment remains gated by product-scope and ADR approval.
openQuestions: Does Google rotate the refresh token during long-lived use, and can agy-auth capture that update atomically per profile?
What at-rest protection should project-owned refresh credentials use?

notRun: Second independently enrolled account, authenticated real-client session, rollback journal, and upgrade behavior were not run.

risks: The contract is reverse engineered and version-specific; refresh credentials are bearer secrets and require protected storage.
doNotRepeat: Do not copy live access tokens; the minimal refresh-token envelope is sufficient.
Do not enable production switching from single-account evidence.
